paragraphs.en: My name is Alice.Early last year, I was troubled by an {anxiety} that crippled ( (削弱) ) my {ability} to do anything.I felt like a {storm cloud hung} over me.For almost a year I struggled on, {constantly} staring at this {wall} that faced me.My perfectionist ( (完美主义者) ) {tendencies} were the main {root} of this: I wanted to be {perfect} at whatever I did, which {obviously} in life is not possible, but it {consumed} me.
paragraphs.cn: 我的名字叫爱丽丝。去年年初，我被 <u> 焦虑 </u> 所困扰，这种焦虑削弱了我做任何事情的 <u> 能力 </u> 。我感觉自己就像被一片 <u> 暴风雨云笼罩 </u> 着。将近一年的时间里，我一直在努力挣扎， <u> 不停地 </u> 注视着这堵横亘在我面前的 <u> 墙 </u> 。我的完美主义 <u> 倾向 </u> 是这一切的主要 <u> 根源 </u> ：我希望自己做任何事都能 <u> 尽善尽美 </u> ，这在现实中 <u> 显然 </u> 是不可能的，但这种想法 <u> 消磨 </u> 着我。

paragraphs.en: One day, I {attended} a presentation by {wildlife} {conservationist} Grant Brown at my high school.His presentation not only {awed} and {inspired} me, but also helped an {inner} desire to make a difference in the world {emerge} .I joined a pre-presentation {dinner} with him and that smaller {setting} allowed me to {slowly} build up my {courage} to speak one-on-one with him—an idea that had seemed {completely} {impossible} .This first contact was where my story began.
paragraphs.cn: 有一天，我在我的高中 <u> 参加 </u> 了一场 <u> 野生动物保护主义者 </u> 格兰特·布朗的演讲。他的演讲不仅 <u> 让 </u> 我 <u> 惊叹 </u> ，使我受到 <u> 鼓舞 </u> ，还使我 <u> 内 </u> 心 <u> 浮现 </u> 出想要改变世界的愿望。我和他一起参加了演讲前的 <u> 晚宴 </u> ，在那个相对较小的 <u> 场合 </u> 里，我得以 <u> 慢慢 </u> 鼓起 <u> 勇气 </u> ，与他进行了一对一的交谈——这在之前似乎是 <u> 完全不可能的 </u> 事情。而这第一次的接触就是我的故事开始的地方。

paragraphs.en: A month later, Brown invited me to attend the World {Youth} Wildlife {Conference} .Looking back, I now see that this would be the first in a {series} of {timely} opportunities that my old self would have let pass, but that this new and more confident Alice {enthusiastically} {seized} .Shortly after I {received} his {invitation} , {applications} to join the Youth for Nature and the Youth for {Planet} groups were sent around through my high school.I decided to {commit} to completing the applications, and soon I was a part of a growing global {team} of young people working to {protect} nature.Each of these new steps continued to grow my confidence.
paragraphs.cn: 一个月后，布朗邀请我参加世界 <u> 青年 </u> 野生动物 <u> 大会 </u> 。如今回想起来，我意识到，这将是一 <u> 系列 </u> 我 <u> 及时 </u> 抓住的机会中的第一个，过去的我可能会错过这些机会，但这个新的、更自信的爱丽丝却 <u> 满怀热情地抓住 </u> 了它们。在我 <u> 收到 </u> 他的 <u> 邀请 </u> 后不久，加入“青年护自然”和“青年护 <u> 地球 </u> ”团体的 <u> 申请 </u> 就在我的高中传开了。我决定 <u> 努力 </u> 完成这些申请，不久，我就成为一个由年轻人组成的、致力于 <u> 保护 </u> 自然，且日益壮大的全球性 <u> 团队 </u> 中的一员。每迈出这样新的一步，我的信心都在不断增强。

paragraphs.en: I am writing this just six months since my journey began, and I've realized that my {biggest obstacle} this whole time was myself.It was that {voice} in the back of my head telling me that one phrase that has stopped so many people from reaching their {potential} : I can't.They say good things come to those who wait; I say: {grab} every opportunity with everything you have and be impatient.After all, nature does not require our patience, but our {action} .
paragraphs.cn: 我写下这些文字时，距离我的旅程开始只过去了六个月，我意识到一直以来我 <u> 最大的障碍 </u> 就是我自己。是我脑海深处的 <u> 声音 </u> 告诉我那句话，正是这句话阻止了许多人发挥他们的 <u> 潜力 </u> ：我做不到。人们常说，好事多磨；而我说，竭尽全力 <u> 抓住 </u> 每一个机会，并且要迫不及待。毕竟，大自然需要的不是我们的耐心，而是我们的 <u> 行动 </u> 。 MKqjwFu4arM4cgPc+LiB66EBg/AaE0u6XBr6IpfU5EiRRdX6Ad+uTD+Kdly4W5UG
